research_question: Does the v0.10 upper-eye family signal survive when rectangular ROIs are replaced by two different glyph-blind anatomical proxy procedures, and do pupil/lower-falcon components independently converge on distinct glyph families?
blindness: Both computational annotation procedures were frozen before any glyph-rank inspection and do not use glyph IDs, fraction values, dates, or fit scores to place masks.

annotators.A: geometric anatomical mask template intersected with the museum-object edge map
annotators.B: edge/Hough-driven detector inside broad anatomical search zones
annotators.critical_limit: These are two distinct computational procedures authored in one workflow. They are not two independent human annotators and do not satisfy the preregistered human-annotation gate.

EYEBROW_UPPER_EYE.interpretation: The previously observed upper-eye signal survives a non-rectangular/dual-method stress test. Both procedures rank multiple D004-D008A eye-family signs near the top while D009/D010 and D011-D016 are not the dominant local matches. This is the strongest replicated layer in the pilot.

HUMAN_EYE_CONTOUR.interpretation: Some eye-family affinity remains but the two mask procedures are not sufficiently concordant for a confirmatory local contour claim.

PUPIL.interpretation: The Hough/circle detector places D012 very high, which is compatible with Unicode's modern D012 classifier-pupil annotation, but the geometric proxy does not replicate it and inter-method mask agreement is effectively zero. This is a method-sensitive canary, not an admitted anatomical mapping.

VERTICAL_FALCON_MARK.interpretation: No stable D011-D016 or eye-family signature survives the two procedures.

DIAGONAL_FALCON_MARK.interpretation: Low inter-method agreement and no frozen lower-family replication; retain as unresolved.

SPIRAL_CURL.interpretation: Both shape procedures are attracted to circular D012-like morphology, demonstrating a strong shape-confound: circularity alone can make a pupil-like glyph rank highly for a spiral. This is a useful false-positive warning, not evidence that D012 encodes the spiral.

source_grounding.MET_547767: The Met explicitly describes a human eye with a horizontal cosmetic line plus a vertical falcon-derived extension and a diagonal line ending in a spiral.
source_grounding.MET_551474: The Met explicitly says the New Kingdom spiral sits directly beneath the cosmetic line, whereas later examples place it much lower.
source_grounding.MET_555588: The Met identifies Wedjat as a combination of human and falcon eye morphology.

highest_admissible_claim: Across five local museum Wedjat images, two distinct glyph-blind computational annotation procedures independently preserve the earlier upper-eye/eyebrow eye-family signal. Detailed pupil and lower falcon-mark/spiral mappings are method-sensitive and fail independent computational replication. The result supports prioritizing a real upper-eye morphology layer, but it does not establish a full multilayer grammar because two genuinely independent human annotations have not yet been collected.

required: object IDs, dates and periods hidden during annotation
all six anatomical components marked without glyph or fraction targets
third annotator only for failed/disputed components
glyph scoring unlocked only after both annotation packages are frozen

execution_provenance.note: The repository implementation preserves the same two-method design; the local execution receipt identifies the exact byte sequence used for the reported pilot.
